title: Configurable Platform for Customer-Specific Workflows
subtitle: Serve ten customers' different fields, approvals, branding and integrations from one stable workflow core, with customisation that is safe, versioned and supportable instead of ten forks.
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Outcome and discovery
practice_prompts.hint: Separate the feature from the outcome, make safe, versioned and supportable testable, and ask the questions that change components.

practice_prompts.label: Peak load and component boundaries
practice_prompts.hint: Show the 42 versus 250 versions-per-hour arithmetic and what it moves: save, validation, deployment, partitioning.

practice_prompts.label: Control plane, data plane and versions
practice_prompts.hint: Trace one tenant change from edit to flagged exposure, and say which record tells you what is live.

practice_prompts.label: Failure policy and the approval loop
practice_prompts.hint: Give detection, containment, recovery and prevention, and the default for each failure type.

practice_prompts.label: Rollout gates and metrics
practice_prompts.hint: Name the four phase gates, the rollback triggers and how fork count and share-handled-by-config are measured.

rubric: Separates the requested feature (configuration) from the outcome (no forks) and makes safe, versioned and supportable testable.
Treats who authors configuration as an architecture decision that changes validation, preview and authorisation.
Sizes for the release-window peak and uses it to split fast saves from queued validation and idempotent deployment.
Separates publishing an immutable version from exposing it behind a tenant flag, and names ConfigDeployment as the record of what is live.
Orders the publish path parse, validate, authorise-by-policy, persist, and explains why it fails closed.
States the idempotency key behaviour: same key and body returns the same deployment, changed body 422, in-flight retry 409.
Contains an infinite approval loop with detection, version freeze, last-known-good recovery and publish-time cycle rejection.
Denies arbitrary code by default and scopes adapters and secrets per tenant.
Rolls out through gated phases and widens configuration only when a second and third customer reuse it without a fork.

editorial_review.evidence: 16 November 2026: read all 46 captured sections (tutorial parts 1-8, coverage notes, takeaways, calibration, sources, 11 worksheet parts, 14 model-answer parts) and all 13 light/dark diagram pairs, then wrote casebook.md from scratch in teach mode. The brief now defines tenant, configuration, fork, control and data plane before using them and adds a labelled illustrative trace that reuses the source's own acme / tpl-9 / version 17 values; the old Tutorial/Worksheet/Model Answer navigation and 70-entry TOC are replaced by the five sections with every old fragment aliased.
